PullRequest.Title: quick input: fix focused item and icon contrast
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- Keep focused Quick Pick and Quick Tree icons in the selection palette instead of retaining an item's inline icon color. Preserve unfocused colors and explicit focused-icon theme overrides.
- Give Light Modern Quick Picks a distinct blue focus background with white text, icons, and search matches, without changing ordinary list selections.
- Apply the focused-match foreground to Quick Trees too, with rendered regression coverage for focus movement and custom colors.

Fixes #348529
Fixes #348530

## Issues addressed

| Severity | Issue | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| Medium | Focused item icons can lose contrast against the selection background (#348529). | Focus styling takes precedence over item-specific inline icon colors. |
| Medium | Light Modern Quick Pick focus is difficult to distinguish (#348530). | Use the theme's existing blue selection palette with readable foregrounds. |
| Medium | The new Light Modern focus background can hide filtered Quick Tree matches. | Use the Quick Input focused-highlight token for Quick Trees as well as Quick Picks. |

Manual checks: in Light 2026, open a session group's **Change Color...** picker and move focus onto **Yellow** with the arrow keys; the focused circle should match the white label, and unfocused circles should retain their colors. In Light Modern, run **Go to Symbol in Editor** in a TypeScript file, type `color`, and move between results; focus and match text should remain clear.

## Review status

- Unresolved actionable findings: None.
- Residual risks: full integration and smoke suites were not run.
- Environment limitation: the isolated baseline dependency bootstrap returned HTTP 401 during postinstall; the installed root dependencies nevertheless built and ran the baseline successfully.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and display a Quick Pick or Quick Tree
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The QuickInputService lazily creates one controller, computes styles, constructs the virtualized list/tree widgets, writes their generated stylesheet text, and displays the picker. The diff adds a constant number of style properties/rules to that existing synchronous UI path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One controller with one list and one tree per service; list/tree item count does not multiply stylesheet generation, and rendered DOM rows are viewport-bounded by ListView virtualization.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized on the UI thread; no queue, worker, IPC, or asynchronous fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The controller is lazily created once and reused. Current theme values are computed on cold controller creation; no new cache key, miss path, negative cache, or coalescing behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: computeStyles, controller updateStyles, DefaultStyleController.style, and virtualized rendering were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact stylesheet parsing and style-recalculation time varies by browser and visible row complexity, but the diff adds only a fixed handful of scoped rules rather than work proportional to total items.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added synchronous work is constant-sized and occurs on existing controller/style initialization, not once per item.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move keyboard focus through filtered Quick Pick and Quick Tree results
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Focus movement updates existing row focus/selection classes, after which the browser matches the new scoped highlight/icon selectors and paints the visible rows. There is no changed JavaScript item traversal or forced geometry read.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Focus-event frequency and the number of currently rendered viewport rows/icons/highlight spans; total backing collection size is bounded out of selector matching by virtualized row rendering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread event and browser style/paint pipeline per focus movement; no burst or parallel work is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved. Browser selector/style caches remain applicable because the stylesheet is stable between theme changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed CSS selectors and list virtualization behavior were inspected, and renderers show icon colors are pre-existing inline styles overridden by CSS.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser-specific selector matching cost is not measured, but selectors are class-scoped, target one focused row, and add only color declarations without layout-affecting properties.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded paint/style matching for the focused visible row and does not introduce collection-wide repeated work, layout, I/O, or allocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load or switch to the Light Modern color theme while quick input exists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold theme activation, the existing theme loader reads and parses light_modern.json and its light_plus.json include; the theme event then recomputes QuickInput styles and replaces two widget stylesheet texts. On a warm already-loaded theme, ColorThemeData.ensureLoaded skips the resource read. The four added color entries are parsed within the same files and do not add another boundary call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the selected JSON color theme and its existing included theme resource through IExtensionResourceLoaderService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two reads for a cold Light Modern activation: light_modern.json and its existing light_plus.json include; zero reads from ensureLoaded once isLoaded is true.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Light Modern file and include were read and parsed; the diff only adds four scalar properties to the existing colors object.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold theme activation awaits the reads and JSON parsing before publishing the theme; this boundary was already on the path and its call count is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected theme file plus its existing single include; four additional scalar color properties. QuickInput restyling is once per theme-change event and independent of item count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Theme loading follows the existing awaited include sequence; QuickInput theme notification/style replacement is serialized on the UI thread. The diff adds no new parallelism or limiter demand.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ColorThemeData.isLoaded avoids subsequent resource reads after successful load. The added color keys use existing color lookup and CSS-variable mechanisms and do not alter cache identity, invalidation, or failure behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed theme file include and ColorThemeData load/read path were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The resource loader may use local filesystem or another extension-resource transport depending on environment, but call cardinality and file topology are unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Cold I/O call count, warm-cache behavior, include depth, and update frequency are unchanged; the additional parse/allocation cost is four bounded scalar entries.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and all diff pages. Traced theme loading, lazy controller creation, dynamic list/tree stylesheet generation, virtualized rendering, and keyboard-focus CSS matching. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or performance-regression fix was found.
